newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols soft, interest in May calls.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols soft, interest in May calls.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options softened after an early rally in underlying bond prices triggered by a smaller than expected rise in the March U.S. consumer price index, dealers said.
Implied volatility for June T-bond futures options was down about 0.4 point at 8.5 percent in late trade, while September fell 0.2 to 9.1 percent.

Still, despite the weakness across the volatility curve, slightly out-of-the-money May 108 calls saw good buying interest as the market's badly bruised sentiment improved somewhat after bonds had the first meaningful bounce.
One house was said to have bought 4,000 lots of the contract early in the day and another firm bought 2,000 in the afternoon. Traders noted a few deals of 500 to 1,000 lots.

"I think they're establishing new positions," said a trader at an investment bank at the Chicago Board of Trade. "People are bulled up about the next few days -- weak numbers lifted the market a full point today, and stocks have also rebounded nicely."
He said it would be interesting to see how much the open interest of the contract, which expires on Friday, had increased today from 23,454 contracts at Monday's close.
Premium on the call was trading at about 57/64 against June futures trading at about 107-21/32 in late trade.

An outright buyer would need June futures to rally close to 108-3/4 this week to break even. But because of May options' high gamma and the edgy bond market environment, delta-hedgers, who can pick up intraday swings in futures, saw the contract to be reasonably cheap, traders said.
"Volatilities are very cheap and everybody's been talking about that the last few days," the bank trader said. May 108 straddles had implied volatility of about eight percent.
June futures were hovering slightly below their highs of 107-27/32 in late trade, up about a point on the day, after rallying early on friendly CPI data.

The overall CPI for March rose 0.1 percent against economists' average forecast of a 0.2 percent gain, while the core CPI excluding food and energy climbed 0.2 percent versus an expected rise of 0.3 percent.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, volatilities for Eurodollar options were steady to easier, also reflecting a CPI-inspired rally in futures.

Implied volatilities for September and December Eurodollar futures options on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange were virtually flat at about 10.1 and 12.0 percent respectively. Mid-curves, which are options expiring in coming months but priced off 1998 futures, were off about 0.2 point each.
An investment bank trader at CME said volatilities were already at historically low levels but seemed likely to plumb still deeper in the near term.
"There's interest to sell everything all the way across the board," he said.
